That night, as the beam swept its slow circle over black water, he imagined every person who might have written those words—a castaway, a child, a lover—and felt, for the first time in months, a little less alone.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市刚刚从梦境的边缘滑出。路灯仍亮着，橘黄色的光晕洒在空无一人的街道上，像一层薄薄的蜜。远处传来环卫车低沉的轰鸣，扫帚划过柏油路面，沙沙作响。早点铺的灯率先亮起，蒸笼里白雾升腾，包子的香气弥漫在潮湿的空气中。一只流浪猫蹲在便利店门口，眯着眼打量偶尔经过的出租车。天际线还是深蓝色的，但东方已隐约泛出一抹鱼肚白。这座城市像一个翻身的睡者，即将醒来，却还舍不得松开最后一缕梦。", "w03": "• Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same problem, like looking up a word in a dictionary and finding the definition uses another word you also need to look up.\n• Every recursive function needs a \"base case\"—a simple version of the problem it can answer right away without calling itself again, so it doesn't keep going forever.\n• Imagine you're in a line of people and you want to know how many are behind you: you ask the person behind you, they ask the person behind them, and so on until the last person says \"zero\"—then each answer gets passed back up the line."}
